prompts.summary: Run a full repository audit with a single report, optionally exported.
prompts.requires: read access to the repository, its documentation and measurement tools
prompts.example: full audit of the repository before the release

prompts.summary: Measure the repository with reproducible metrics and find hotspots.
prompts.requires: read access to the repository, its Git history and measurement tools
prompts.example: metrics and hotspots of the repository

prompts.summary: Audit architecture and technical debt not yet tracked.
prompts.requires: read access to the code, the backlog and architecture documentation
prompts.example: audit of architecture and technical debt of the repository

prompts.summary: Audit dependencies: outdated, vulnerable and unused.
prompts.requires: manifests, lock files and access to package registries or dependency advisories
prompts.example: dependency audit before the upgrade

prompts.summary: Audit the CI/CD pipeline and supply chain
prompts.requires: Pipeline definitions, workflow permissions, secrets handling, third-party actions and release process
prompts.example: AUD07: audit the GitHub Actions workflows for unpinned actions and excess permissions

prompts.summary: Explore the repository and identify main components and commands.
prompts.requires: read access to the repository and a shell
prompts.example: explore the structure and main modules

prompts.summary: Trace a flow and its dependencies through the code.
prompts.requires: entry point or scenario to trace
prompts.example: trace the authentication and session flow

prompts.summary: Find official sources that fit the technical problem.
prompts.requires: technical problem or library with its version
prompts.example: find the official documentation for the runtime version in use

prompts.summary: Assess the impact, risks and dependencies of a change.
prompts.requires: proposed change or defect to fix
prompts.example: assess the impact of isolating runtime logs

prompts.summary: Analyze logs and incidents to find the root cause, without changing code.
prompts.requires: logs, errors or symptoms of the incident, time window and read access
prompts.example: find the root cause of yesterday's errors in the logs

prompts.summary: Explain code or a concept to someone new to the project
prompts.requires: The code, module or concept to explain and the reader's starting level
prompts.example: COM06: explain how the payment retry flow works to a new teammate

prompts.summary: Migrate schema and data with verifiable comparison and recovery.
prompts.requires: source schema, target schema and synthetic data
prompts.example: migrate the schema with an atomic rollback script

prompts.summary: Build imports and transformations that preserve the originals.
prompts.requires: source files, target model and validation rules
prompts.example: import the catalog from CSV to JSON preserving the originals

prompts.summary: Integrate API services with error handling and request retries.
prompts.requires: API documentation, test credentials and schema
prompts.example: implement a REST client with exponential backoff and retry

prompts.summary: Optimize database queries and indexes
prompts.requires: Slow queries or endpoints, schema, indexes, execution plans and a safe test database
prompts.example: DAT04: speed up the orders listing query without changing its results

prompts.summary: Implement a feature with relevant checks.
prompts.requires: verified requirements or acceptance criteria
prompts.example: implement the export command with hash validation

prompts.summary: Triage a defect report, reproduce it and fix its cause.
prompts.requires: report or expected and actual behavior
prompts.example: triage and fix the parsing error for paths containing spaces; triage only, no fix

prompts.summary: Refactor code preserving contracts: targeted, phased or periodic.
prompts.requires: code to improve, existing tests and scope (targeted, phased or periodic)
prompts.example: extract transaction handling into its own module

prompts.summary: Update dependencies checking compatibility and regressions.
prompts.requires: dependency manifests and lock files
prompts.example: update the JSON serialization package

prompts.summary: Migrate code or a framework to a defined target.
prompts.requires: source and target versions with release notes
prompts.example: migrate the scripts from the old runtime version to the current one

prompts.summary: Configure and run linters, formatters and static analysis.
prompts.requires: linter configuration and analysis scope
prompts.example: configure the linter and run static analysis

prompts.summary: Build or review an LLM feature with evaluations
prompts.requires: The LLM or agent feature, model and provider, expected behavior, failure cases and sample inputs
prompts.example: DEV12: add an evaluation set for the support bot before changing its prompt

prompts.summary: Write guides and READMEs consistent with the real product.
prompts.requires: implemented features, verified commands and approved screenshots
prompts.example: update the guides and add Mermaid flow diagrams

prompts.summary: Document APIs and contracts from the implementation.
prompts.requires: source code of the contracts and endpoints
prompts.example: document the parameters and response schemas of the endpoints

prompts.summary: Capture real screenshots and prepare public assets.
prompts.requires: working interface with synthetic data
prompts.example: capture authentic screenshots from the real interface

prompts.summary: Write or update an operational runbook
prompts.requires: The procedure, systems involved, access needed, failure modes and an operator who can validate it
prompts.example: DOC04: write a runbook for restoring the database from backup

prompts.summary: Create diagrams, posters, infographics and social or site flows from real code
prompts.requires: real code or the stated project intent, the audience and channel (social, site, marketing, docs) and the format
prompts.example: DOC05: draw the architecture diagram and a one-page infographic of the runner from the code

prompts.summary: Survey a repository and propose its specific agent directives
prompts.requires: the checkout, the global and common directive blocks, the current AGENTS.md and dossier directives, the startup budget
prompts.example: DOC06: survey this repository and propose the directives agents need here beyond the common blocks

prompts.summary: Verify licenses and compatibility and keep the CREDITS register up to date.
prompts.requires: dependency lock files, manifests, vendored code and third-party licenses
prompts.example: check licenses and SPDX headers and update CREDITS.md

prompts.summary: Assess usability, consistency and states of user flows.
prompts.requires: runnable application and flows to examine
prompts.example: assess the usability of the setup wizard

prompts.summary: Implement an interface following requirements and references.
prompts.requires: guidelines or mockups and existing components
prompts.example: build the synchronization screen

prompts.summary: Verify accessibility and keyboard and assistive-technology use.
prompts.requires: working interface and reference standards
prompts.example: verify ARIA conformance and accessibility

prompts.summary: Verify internationalization of strings, formats and translations.
prompts.requires: interface or messages with supported languages and formats
prompts.example: verify the strings, formats and translations of the CLI

prompts.summary: Write or review interface copy and error messages
prompts.requires: Screens or flows, audience, tone, existing terminology and supported languages
prompts.example: INT05: rewrite the checkout error messages so each says what to do next

prompts.summary: Align local instructions, context, memory and tracker.
prompts.requires: recent decisions or changes not yet recorded
prompts.example: sb prompt MEM01: align context.md and memory.md after completing a task

prompts.summary: Migrate design and tasks into the SecondBrain dossier.
prompts.requires: historical documentation or external issues to migrate
prompts.example: sb prompt MEM02: migrate scattered todos into the dossier's central tracker

prompts.summary: Close the session: memories, tracker, handoff and commit and push request.
prompts.requires: state of the work done, defined next tasks and delivery destination
prompts.example: sb prompt MEM03: close the session and ask for commit and push

prompts.summary: Create, update and archive projects, areas and resources of the central PARA.
prompts.requires: goal of the PARA entity and a write session on the SecondBrain clone
prompts.example: sb prompt MEM05: archive the finished resource res-guida

prompts.summary: Read memory, context and tracker of the current repository and list its tasks.
prompts.requires: checkout of the open repository
prompts.example: sb prompt MEM06: load the repository context and list the ready tasks

prompts.summary: Resume work stopped by a usage limit, importing it from another account
prompts.requires: the stopped work (MEM09 or MEM03 report, runner resume.json, branch or worktree) and the import method the person picks
prompts.example: MEM07: the runner stopped for quota on the other account, import its work and continue the task

prompts.summary: Start a session: context, repository state, alignment and next tasks
prompts.requires: any folder; a managed repository adds the dossier, the tracker and the alignment check
prompts.example: MEM08: start the session in this repository and propose the next tasks

prompts.summary: Stop the agent, save the session and hand it over to another IDE or account
prompts.requires: the task in progress, the Git state of the checkout and the person's choice for uncommitted work
prompts.example: sb stop: I am at the end of my weekly limit, save the session so I can resume from another account

prompts.summary: Prepare and verify distributable packages and artifacts.
prompts.requires: build instructions and package requirements
prompts.example: build a deterministic zip archive and compute its SHA-256

prompts.summary: Configure pipelines, containers and infrastructure as code.
prompts.requires: deployment requirements and target environment
prompts.example: configure a multi-stage Dockerfile for a reproducible build

prompts.summary: Add logs, metrics and diagnostics useful for the problem.
prompts.requires: scenario to monitor and logging standards
prompts.example: add structured JSON logging

prompts.summary: Prepare release notes and delivery checks.
prompts.requires: commits, issues or tasks completed since the previous release
prompts.example: compile the v1.1 release notes from commits and issues

prompts.summary: Prepare commits and pull requests with verified scope, message and checks.
prompts.requires: local changes to deliver and an explicit request for a commit or pull request
prompts.example: prepare the commits and the pull request description

prompts.summary: Prepare a release hotfix and rollback with verification and communication.
prompts.requires: faulty release, known previous version and criteria for going back
prompts.example: prepare the hotfix and rollback for release 2.3.1

prompts.summary: Write a blameless incident postmortem
prompts.requires: Incident timeline, impact, logs or alerts, the fix applied and the people involved
prompts.example: OPS07: write the postmortem for last night's checkout outage

prompts.summary: Turn a request into requirements and acceptance criteria.
prompts.requires: user request and existing documentation
prompts.example: define acceptance criteria for full-text search

prompts.summary: Compare architectural options and justify a decision.
prompts.requires: alternatives to evaluate and project constraints
prompts.example: compare SQLite and JSON for local persistence

prompts.summary: Design API contracts, data models and compatibility.
prompts.requires: requirements or current schema with its version
prompts.example: design the JSON schema and API contracts for the task list

prompts.summary: Prepare a phased plan with dependencies, checks and rollback.
prompts.requires: agreed requirements and scope of the work; for a restructuring, the target structure and test coverage
prompts.example: plan the migration in three atomic releases; plan the split of the data module

prompts.summary: Scaffold new modules with structure, configuration and tests.
prompts.requires: agreed architectural scope and dependencies
prompts.example: define the scaffolding of the new module

prompts.summary: Record an architecture decision (ADR)
prompts.requires: The decision made or to make, its context, constraints, options considered and who decides
prompts.example: PRG07: record why we chose PostgreSQL over MongoDB

prompts.summary: Complete the next ready task of the open repository.
prompts.requires: planned task and acceptance criteria
prompts.example: run the next priority task that can be done autonomously

prompts.summary: Remove leftovers and unused code; align .gitignore and .gitkeep.
prompts.requires: proof of no references and green tests; tracked and ignored file lists
prompts.example: remove temporary files and orphaned build caches and fix the ignore rules

prompts.summary: Inspect the repo and find leftover tasks against the real code.
prompts.requires: working tree, recent history and any backlog or notes
prompts.example: inspect the repo and detect leftover tasks

prompts.summary: Report an error as GitHub issues in the form format, after confirmation.
prompts.requires: observed error, reproduction steps, version and `gh` authenticated
prompts.example: report this build error as a GitHub issue

prompts.summary: Consolidate branches with a --no-ff merge and delete the integrated ones.
prompts.requires: local and remote branches, the base branch and a clean working tree
prompts.example: consolidate the finished branches into master

prompts.summary: Align the GitHub page, community files and security, after confirmation.
prompts.requires: `gh` authenticated with admin rights and a SEC07 result
prompts.example: make this repository discoverable and apply standard security

prompts.summary: Triage open issues and pull requests
prompts.requires: GitHub repository with gh authenticated, labels, project rules, age and activity of issues and PRs
prompts.example: REP14: triage open issues and PRs and propose labels and closures

prompts.summary: Run ready autonomous tasks with the runner, monitor and record the outcome
prompts.requires: ready autonomous tasks, the desktop runner (scripts/runner.ps1) or the command line (run-ready-tasks.ps1, launcher) and the user's go-ahead for -Run
prompts.example: REP15: run the ready autonomous tasks, follow the run and record the outcome

prompts.summary: Unblock blocked tasks: verify the real reason, then make them autonomous
prompts.requires: tracker with blocked tasks, their state reasons and acceptance criteria, and the answers of the user to a structured interview
prompts.example: REP16: review the blocked tasks and make the ones without a real prerequisite autonomous

prompts.summary: Reorder the tracker, archive done tasks and put qualifications after development
prompts.requires: tracker with its archive, the priority scheme chosen by the user and the list of tasks with real prerequisites
prompts.example: REP17: archive the done tasks and move qualifications below development

prompts.summary: Analyze a non-runnable task and ask what makes it autonomous
prompts.requires: one task the runner skips, its reason and dependencies, the checkout read-only and the owner's answers to multiple-choice questions
prompts.example: REP18: analyze task #42 and ask me only what is needed to make it autonomous

prompts.summary: Review changes or code for correctness, security and maintainability.
prompts.requires: diff, commit or files to analyze
prompts.example: review the pull request for data leaks; review the readability of the parser module

prompts.summary: Analyze threats, trust boundaries and abuse scenarios.
prompts.requires: architecture and data flows toward the outside
prompts.example: threat model of the stdio and local file system flows

prompts.summary: Fix vulnerabilities and strengthen the affected defenses.
prompts.requires: confirmed vulnerability and code context
prompts.example: fix path traversal in path resolution

prompts.summary: Find exposed credentials and verify input validation.
prompts.requires: working tree and scanning tools
prompts.example: run a credentials security audit

prompts.summary: Verify personal data isolation and compliance with GDPR and policies.
prompts.requires: data mapping and compliance policy
prompts.example: check for personal data and GDPR privacy compliance

prompts.summary: Harden repository configuration, CI, containers and access.
prompts.requires: configuration, CI workflows, containers and repository settings
prompts.example: harden the GitHub Actions workflows and containers

prompts.summary: Check for sensitive data before publishing, locally and on the remote
prompts.requires: Commits, index, working tree and history to publish; remote destination and visibility; scanning tools available
prompts.example: SEC07: check the commits about to be pushed, and the remote, for sensitive data

prompts.summary: Wipe remote GitHub history and artifacts after a data exposure.
prompts.requires: explicit request, verified backup and administrative access to the remote
prompts.example: wipe the remote history, runs and caches after the exposure

prompts.summary: Check the IDEs; map, register accounts or realign on request.
prompts.requires: IDE installations and local authorizations; to register accounts also an activated workstation and consent
prompts.example: sb prompt SYS01: register an ide with two accounts or two roots

prompts.summary: Check authoritative sources; acquire or update on request.
prompts.requires: PARA resource-authoritative-sources registry
prompts.example: sb prompt SYS02: check regulatory updates in the sources registry

prompts.summary: Activate SecondBrain after discovery and asset selection.
prompts.requires: SecondBrain volume and user consent on the assets
prompts.example: sb prompt SYS03: activate secondbrain selecting local repositories and ides

prompts.summary: Check or align the workstation's already managed assets.
prompts.requires: workstation configuration and approved directives
prompts.example: sb prompt SYS04: check directive alignment in the managed repositories

prompts.summary: Compact the dossier preserving originals, facts and TOC.
prompts.requires: dossier to compact and verifiable history
prompts.example: sb prompt SYS05: compact the dossier history preserving facts and toc

prompts.summary: Run the deterministic compressed backup and verify the SHA-256 digests.
prompts.requires: active configuration and backup runtime root
prompts.example: sb prompt SYS09: run a deterministic backup and validate the sha-256 manifest

prompts.summary: Roll back and decommission a repository, returning its data for privacy.
prompts.requires: repository dossier, target checkout and user consent
prompts.example: sb prompt SYS10: roll back the decommissioned repository and clean up the data

prompts.summary: Add, change or remove a prompt of the centralized catalog.
prompts.requires: valid catalog, target area and a write session
prompts.example: sb prompt SYS11: add a prompt to the catalog in the test area

prompts.summary: Set or remove the greenfield lock (versions, changelog, migrations, aliases).
prompts.requires: managed repository, active dossier and user confirmation
prompts.example: sb prompt SYS13: set or remove the greenfield lock on this repository

prompts.summary: Install the SecondBrain MCP server in the IDEs and verify the handshake.
prompts.requires: SecondBrain root, target IDEs and confirmation before writing
prompts.example: sb prompt SYS15: install the mcp server in vscode and claude code

prompts.summary: Update a skill from authoritative sources and verify the diff.
prompts.requires: identified skill, target agent and version, official sources
prompts.example: sb prompt SYS16: update the local skill from official sources

prompts.summary: Guide the first-run setup of SecondBrain, IDE, agent, directives and MCP.
prompts.requires: fresh SecondBrain checkout, one supported IDE and confirmation before each write
prompts.example: sb setup: configure this clean workstation with vscode

prompts.summary: Analyze a project, propose skills and install the selected ones
prompts.requires: a project checkout, the agents and scope to install into, and confirmation before each write
prompts.example: sb skills: analyze this project and install the useful skills for claude-code and codex

prompts.summary: Add unit and integration tests for the relevant risks.
prompts.requires: test harness and the behavior to verify
prompts.example: add boundary tests for the budget calculation

prompts.summary: Cover user journeys with end-to-end tests.
prompts.requires: test environment and agreed user flows
prompts.example: create an end-to-end test for the backup and restore cycle

prompts.summary: Find and fix flaky or non-deterministic tests.
prompts.requires: logs of the intermittent failures and the test suite
prompts.example: fix the instability in the async tests of the suite

prompts.summary: Diagnose and fix build and test failures in CI.
prompts.requires: CI logs and pipeline configuration
prompts.example: fix the GitHub Actions runner failure on Windows

prompts.summary: Verify real behavior against the requirements.
prompts.requires: acceptance criteria and a working environment
prompts.example: verify that the output conforms to the specifications

prompts.summary: Audit or optimize performance and resources, measuring before and after.
prompts.requires: flow, representative load, environment, metric and threshold
prompts.example: find the critical paths of host discovery, then reduce time and memory use

prompts.summary: Set up a test harness with isolated fixtures and safe cleanup.
prompts.requires: test framework, test scripts and an assigned isolated fixture root
prompts.example: create isolated on-disk fixtures and validate the automatic cleanup

prompts.summary: Review test quality and find coverage gaps
prompts.requires: Test suite, coverage reports if any, critical paths and recent defects
prompts.example: TST08: review the billing module tests for gaps and weak assertions

prompts.summary: Define the requirements, audience and success criteria of a site or app
prompts.requires: a brief of the site or app, its audience and constraints, and write access to the docs folder
prompts.example: WEB01: define the requirements and success criteria of the new company website

prompts.summary: Choose the stack, hosting and architecture of a site or app with trade-offs
prompts.requires: the requirements (WEB01), team skills, budget and hosting constraints
prompts.example: WEB02: compare stacks and hosting for the new site and record the decision

prompts.summary: Design information architecture, user flows, content and a small design system
prompts.requires: the requirements (WEB01), the chosen architecture and any brand assets
prompts.example: WEB03: design the sitemap, key flows and design tokens for the new site

prompts.summary: Scaffold the project and build a first working vertical slice
prompts.requires: architecture and design decisions, an empty or new repository and a working toolchain
prompts.example: WEB04: scaffold the project and deliver the first page end to end with tests

prompts.summary: Develop the remaining features in phases with tests and accessibility checks
prompts.requires: the first vertical slice (WEB04), a phased backlog and a working test setup
prompts.example: WEB05: build the next phase of features and verify tests and accessibility

prompts.summary: Prepare release, hosting, monitoring, backups and handover of a site or app
prompts.requires: a built and tested application, the hosting target and the delivery owner
prompts.example: WEB06: prepare the production release, monitoring and handover notes

prompts.summary: Assess company AI use cases, data readiness and feasibility, then rank them
prompts.requires: a description of the business processes and data, and the stakeholders to interview
prompts.example: AIS01: assess where AI fits in our company and rank the use cases

prompts.summary: Design a local inference system: models, hardware, serving, scaling and limits
prompts.requires: the chosen use case (AIS01), data sensitivity, available hardware and latency targets
prompts.example: AIS02: design the on-premises inference service for the support use case

prompts.summary: Connect inference to business applications and production systems safely
prompts.requires: the inference service (AIS02), the API or database of the target application and an agreed owner
prompts.example: AIS03: connect the local model to the ERP and the production line dashboard

prompts.summary: Build a local-AI chatbot to embed in an existing website
prompts.requires: the existing site and its stack, a local model endpoint (AIS02), the knowledge sources and the tone of voice
prompts.example: AIS04: add a local-AI chatbot widget to our existing website

prompts.summary: Design retrieval (RAG) over company documents with access control and evals
prompts.requires: the document sources, their permissions and a set of real questions to answer
prompts.example: AIS05: design retrieval over the company manuals and test it on real questions

prompts.summary: Evaluate, monitor and operate an AI system in production
prompts.requires: a running AI feature, a representative evaluation set and access to its logs
prompts.example: AIS06: set up evaluation, monitoring and a rollback plan for the chatbot

prompts.summary: Assess AI privacy, security and compliance (GDPR, AI Act, prompt injection)
prompts.requires: the AI system design, the data it processes and the jurisdiction
prompts.example: AIS07: assess privacy, security and compliance risks of the company chatbot

prompts.summary: Estimate cost, ROI and an adoption and training plan for company AI
prompts.requires: the ranked use cases (AIS01), expected volumes and the current process cost
prompts.example: AIS08: estimate cost and return of the chatbot and plan staff adoption

prompts.summary: Automate a business process with AI agents, tools and human review
prompts.requires: a documented process, the systems it touches and the people who approve exceptions
prompts.example: AIS09: automate invoice triage with an AI agent and human approval

prompts.summary: Analyze the repository and propose authoritative skills for the project
prompts.requires: read access to the repository and its manifests, and official skill sources to consult
prompts.example: COM07: analyze this repository and propose the skills that would support it

prompts.summary: Analyze project intent, limits, production fit and known alternatives
prompts.requires: the repository (code, README, dossier) and access to official sources of the comparable projects
prompts.example: COM08: what this project solves, what it cannot, where it fits in production and how it differs from known tools

prompts.summary: Harden a website: headers, TLS, forms, admin, dependencies and abuse limits
prompts.requires: the site code and configuration, its hosting target and write access to the repository
prompts.example: WEB07: harden the company website before the public launch

prompts.summary: Verify and update site indexing: sitemap, robots, webmaster tools, schema
prompts.requires: the live or staging site, the domain owner's access to the search tools, write access to the repository
prompts.example: WEB08: verify what is indexed and update sitemap, robots and webmaster tools

prompts.summary: Control AI crawlers and bots: robots rules, verification, rate limits, logs
prompts.requires: the site, its access logs or CDN/WAF console and the owner's policy on AI use of content
prompts.example: WEB09: block AI training crawlers on the site and verify the rules in the logs

prompts.summary: Plan a SecondBrain maintenance round and choose the routines to run
prompts.requires: read access to the checkout, the dossier tracker and the latest reports in history
prompts.example: MNT01: plan this week's maintenance round and list what is due

prompts.summary: Health check: directives, IDEs, prompts, tests and publication scan
prompts.requires: the SecondBrain checkout, PowerShell 7.5+ and Git
prompts.example: MNT02: run the health check and report what drifted

prompts.summary: Tidy the dossier: archive done tasks, compact, reorder and sync
prompts.requires: write access to the dossiers through the coordinated writer and a recent backup
prompts.example: MNT03: tidy the SecondBrain dossier after the last release

prompts.summary: Verify backups with a real restore test and report coverage gaps
prompts.requires: the backup archives, the manifest and an empty scratch folder for the restore
prompts.example: MNT04: test the latest backup by restoring it into a scratch folder

prompts.summary: Review .runtime and clean up in preview; apply only with authorization
prompts.requires: the checkout, no active sessions and the owner's authorization before any deletion
prompts.example: MNT05: report what .runtime holds and propose the cleanup preview

prompts.summary: Refresh authoritative sources, skills and tool versions and verify the diff
prompts.requires: network access to official sources and the registered sources and skills of the workstation
prompts.example: MNT06: check the registered sources and skills for updates

prompts.summary: Prepare a directive revision: proposal, preview, version, changelog, checks
prompts.requires: a concrete change to the common directives and the owner's approval path
prompts.example: MNT07: prepare the revision proposal for the new common directive

prompts.summary: Reconcile conflicting or invalid queued writes and orphan receipts.
prompts.requires: a managed repository and a write session to apply
prompts.example: sb reconcile tasks: plan the queued conflicts of this repository
